item: Receiving and intermediary bank fees
why: No official page publishes what a U.S. receiving bank or a correspondent bank charges. Every total on this page excludes them.
what_would_settle_it: Your U.S. bank's incoming-wire fee schedule and the correspondent bank named on a test wire.

item: FBAR penalty amounts may have been adjusted again in 2026
why: The eCFR text read today still shows the amounts effective for penalties assessed on or after 17 January 2025 (90 FR 5630). If FinCEN published a 2026 inflation adjustment, the eCFR read today does not yet show it.
what_would_settle_it: The Federal Register document for the 2026 adjustment, and FinCEN's penalty page.

item: Two thresholds for reporting a foreign gift
why: The statute says information is required once aggregate foreign gifts exceed USD 10,000, while IRS guidance requires Form 3520 Part IV only above USD 100,000 for gifts from a nonresident alien or foreign estate.
what_would_settle_it: Form 3520 instructions for the relevant year, and a preparer's reading of the regulation behind the USD 100,000 figure.

item: One rate snapshot
why: Every figure is priced at the BOC board published 2026/11/11 10:25:02 (USD selling 669.11 per 100). The board changes during the day, so a quote taken later will differ.
what_would_settle_it: A fresh board reading and a rebuild, or the branch's own quote.

item: The 50,000-a-year route assumes one rate for eight years
why: The cost line multiplies today's rate and today's fee across eight tranches. That is arithmetic, not a forecast of rates or fees.
what_would_settle_it: Treat the number as the cost at today's prices only.

item: The card route uses the bank board rate as a stand-in
why: The conversion rate applied by the card network is not published on any page read today. The bank's USD selling rate is used instead, and the ATM owner's own fee is not included.
what_would_settle_it: The card network's published conversion rule and a foreign ATM receipt.

item: The cash route excludes most of its real cost
why: Only the exchange margin is priced. Travel, insurance, any banknote withdrawal fee, and the fact that above USD 10,000 a SAFE permit is needed and in principle not granted, are outside the figure.
what_would_settle_it: A bank quote for banknote purchase and the permit rules at the branch.

item: Your branch may not charge the published tariff
why: BOC's tariff page says agreements, discounts and local fee differences are charged per the agreement or the local published schedule.
what_would_settle_it: The branch's own fee schedule in writing.

item: The change-back route dies with the slip
why: The 24-month change-back right depends on the original exchange slip. If it is lost and the bank cannot reprint it, that route is gone.
what_would_settle_it: The branch's answer on reprinting 水单 from its records.

item: Your U.S. basis is unknown
why: The currency-gain column is an illustration using IRS yearly averages for 2024 and 2025. Your actual §988 gain depends on when and at what rate you acquired the RMB, and on whether the transaction is personal.
what_would_settle_it: Your acquisition statements and a preparer's §988 computation.

item: Treaty rate on dividends not read
why: The dividend row is priced at the statutory 20 % only. Article 9 of the treaty was not read today, so no treaty rate is stated.
what_would_settle_it: The treaty text and a preparer's view.

item: Foreign tax credit not verified
why: No claim is made about crediting Chinese tax against U.S. tax, because the rule was not read from an official page today.
what_would_settle_it: IRS Publication 514 and the Form 1116 instructions.

item: Gifted or undocumented money has no verified route
why: No official page read today allows a foreign passport holder to convert RMB received as a gift, or RMB whose origin cannot be documented; the 2004 measure expressly refuses applications that cannot prove a lawful source.
what_would_settle_it: A written answer from the SAFE branch responsible for the account, after stating the facts.

item: The 'considerable taxes' were never identified
why: The brief names no tax, rate, amount or assessing office. Nothing read today taxes the conversion itself, so the number in the brief may be Chinese income tax, U.S. income tax on the currency gain, or a misunderstanding.
what_would_settle_it: The notice or quote, with the article relied on and the amount.

item: Local practice decides
why: Two official definitions of domestic individual exist (the Regulation counts a foreigner resident for one continuous year; SAFE's own Q&As speak of foreign individuals under art 59). Which one the branch applies, and what documents it demands, varies.
what_would_settle_it: A written answer from the branch and, if needed, from the SAFE branch that supervises it.

item: Money-transfer companies and apps
why: No page read today confirms that any named remittance company or app can lawfully move a personal RMB balance out of the mainland. None is recommended here.
what_would_settle_it: The company's licence, its regulator, and its published terms for mainland China.

item: The 2004 transfer measure is old
why: The 2004 PBOC measure still governs emigrant and inheritance transfers, but later notices adjust how it is applied. Those later texts were not read in full today.
what_would_settle_it: The SAFE branch's current operating checklist.

item: Landing page attributes the 30 % fine to the wrong source
why: index.html says quotas, private swaps and crypto are 'prohibited, with fines of up to 30 % of the amount' and cites S05, S06, S10 and S21. None of those four pages contains a fine (S10 is the watchlist answer, read today). The 30 % is in Regulation arts 39, 40 and 45, which that card does not cite.
what_would_settle_it: Add the Regulation (S17) to that card's citations, or drop the fine clause.

item: Nine legacy pages cite a repealed crypto notice
why: 银发〔2021〕237号 was repealed on 2026-02-06 by 银发〔2026〕42号. The canonical dashboard cites the 2026 notice; nine older pages still cite the 2021 one. The prohibition is unchanged in substance, so this is a citation defect, not a wrong answer.
what_would_settle_it: Point those pages at the 2026 notice when they are next revised, or leave them archived and labelled.

item: The dashboard is priced one board behind
why: The dashboard prices the 10 November board (selling 668.51). Today's board is 669.11, so its headline figures are USD 53.38 / 899.01 against USD 53.42 / 901.20 today - a 0.07-0.24 % difference. Its own flag U15 records this. This page publishes the repriced ladder rather than editing another session's data.
what_would_settle_it: A rebuild of the dashboard from a fresh board reading.

item: Board's 'Middle Rate' column is not the midpoint
why: The board shows selling 669.11, buying 666.30 and 'Middle Rate' 671.91. The midpoint of buying and selling is 667.705. This page's fair value is its own midpoint and says so.
what_would_settle_it: None needed; recorded so the two columns are not confused.
